findings.potential_impact: An authorized migration can change or destroy target data; bypassed authority or an overprivileged target role would magnify the impact.
findings.rationale: Executing approved SQL is the platform feature: arbitrary DDL cannot be replaced by a parameter placeholder. The engine reparses one allowed statement and verifies protected metadata; the worker revalidates immutable SQL hashes, editor permission and every required leader approval. Provision restricted target credentials. This is an intentional SQL sink with residual operational risk, not a claim that user SQL is harmless.

findings.message: This operation, which is used in an [allocation](1), involves a [potentially large value](2) and might overflow.
findings.potential_impact: Integer overflow or excessive LCS allocation could panic a schema-diff request; summed capacities also lacked explicit bounds.
findings.rationale: Bound dimensions before +1, guard the product by division against two million cells, use a linear fallback, and remove summed capacity hints. A 12000-line asymmetric regression passes. All nine instances are absent from the rescan.

findings.decision: false positive in configured JSON sinks
findings.potential_impact: Raw control characters in text logging could forge records or hide audit events.
findings.rationale: Both the workflow default logger and production Configure use slog JSON handlers. Dynamic fields are encoded as JSON data, control characters are escaped, event names are code-defined, and correlatedHandler redacts attributes before console/OTLP fan-out. No raw user string is concatenated into a line-oriented text record. Custom consumers must preserve structured encoding.

findings.message: Code construction depends on an [improperly sanitized value](1).
findings.decision: false positive in test-only CDP helper
findings.potential_impact: Unsafe JavaScript string construction could execute unintended code in the test browser.
findings.rationale: click/field/check interpolate JSON.stringify(value) as a complete JavaScript string literal, passed directly to DevTools Runtime.evaluate, not into HTML or a script element. Callers supply repository-controlled test strings. Quotes and backslashes are encoded; no external request supplies a code fragment. These helpers are not part of either shipped SPA.

findings.message: Outbound network request depends on [file data](1).
findings.potential_impact: An attacker-controlled port file could redirect a test browser control request to another local port.
findings.rationale: Chrome writes DevToolsActivePort in a private mkdtemp profile created by this test. The outbound host is fixed to 127.0.0.1 and the file belongs to the trusted child browser. A local actor able to replace private fixture files is outside this isolated test trust boundary. No production endpoint exposes this flow.

findings.message: Write to file system depends on [Untrusted data](1).
findings.decision: false positive for fixed JSON diagnostic
findings.potential_impact: Network-controlled filesystem paths or executable file contents could overwrite files or introduce code.
findings.rationale: The timeout diagnostic writes JSON.stringify of browser text/error data to a fixed timeout.json under the chosen evidence directory. Page content cannot choose the path and remains inert JSON data. The helper runs only in the local UI test harness, not a public HTTP handler.
